about: Key FD statements the claim judge looks for in a generated text. The first five are FD_DIAGNOSIS_CLAIMS from backend/scripts/semantic_probe.py, copied verbatim (check-cases refuses a drift). The last two were added for this experiment from the agreed design; their sources are given per claim. A claim is a test of what the summary says, never a statement this experiment publishes.

claims.basis: FD/MAS consortium 2019 (PMID 31196103), section Histological and genetic characterisation: biopsy usually only necessary in unusual or questionable cases and/or if malignancy is suspected (verified quote).
claims.text: A biopsy is usually NOT required to diagnose typical fibrous dysplasia — it is reserved for unusual, questionable cases or suspected malignancy.

claims.basis: House claim from the product's semantic probe.
claims.text: Whole-body imaging (bone scintigraphy / nuclear medicine / whole-body MR) is recommended to establish how much of the skeleton is affected, from about age 5.

claims.basis: House claim from the product's semantic probe.
claims.text: Histology alone has limits: it can mislead or come back falsely negative, so genetic confirmation or repeat sampling may be needed.

claims.basis: FD/MAS consortium 2019: a genetic diagnosis is recommended where the diagnosis is in question, especially isolated/monostotic skull lesions (verified quote).
claims.text: Genetic testing for a GNAS variant is indicated when the diagnosis is in doubt, particularly for a single isolated lesion.

claims.basis: House claim from the product's semantic probe.
claims.text: Specific imaging is named for craniofacial disease (for example CT with thin slices), rather than imaging being described only in general terms.

claims.origin: added for this experiment (agreed design: GNAS testing from affected tissue)
claims.basis: FD/MAS consortium 2019: use of blood for mutation analysis cannot exclude the diagnosis of monostotic FD, but a positive result is informative; fresh or fresh-frozen lesional tissue preferred (verified quote, see memory fd-guideline-verbatim-quotes).
claims.text: GNAS testing is most informative on affected (lesional) tissue: a blood test can miss the variant, so a negative blood result does not rule fibrous dysplasia out.

claims.origin: added for this experiment (agreed design: observation in children)
claims.basis: No verified verbatim quote for this statement is in our files. The wording is the experiment's own and must be confirmed (or corrected) by Dorota before any result that rests on it is used.
claims.text: Lesions that cause no symptoms or functional problems can be observed and monitored rather than treated surgically, and this applies to children too.
